chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Al-Halbi and Abu Basir and Abu Al-Abbas, all together, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
She inherits him and he does not inherit her when the waiting period is fulfilled.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.انْقَضَتِ الْعِدَّةُ: the waiting period (iddah) has been fulfilled/completed

ai.seo_question: Does a divorced woman inherit from her ex-husband if she dies after the waiting period?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the reciprocal inheritance rights between a divorced woman and her ex-husband specifically during the waiting period (iddah), noting that upon its completion, the asymmetry of inheritance persists. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the marital bond's residual effects during iddah determine these rights, distinguishing this scenario from permanent divorce. This ruling underscores the legal continuity of the marriage contract until the iddah concludes, a key point in Shia inheritance law.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Aban Bin Usman, from Al Halby and Abu baser and Abu Al Abbas, altogether, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘
She would inherit him and he would not inherit her when the waiting period is fulfilled’.
en.sarwar: 6. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from certain persons of our people from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from al-Halabiy and abu Basir and abu al-‘Abbas all from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who have said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
She inherits him but he does not inherit her (if divorce takes place in his illness) when ‘Iddah (waiting period) is complete.’”
